messages.author: 936ef8c6d12fc338
messages.subject: numerical errors with random walks
parts:
Dear all,

In this small example the models m0 and m1 fit fine while the models with random walk have numerical errors. Any idea what is going wrong? Setting an informative prior doesn't fix the problem. I'm running INLA version 22.03.06.

Best regards,

Thierry

ds <- data.frame(
  x = 1:21,
  y = c(
    59.8399024898837, 56.8269219894829, 56.2146544693856, 53.2833353115139,
    48.308128754171, 47.3959150343844, 47.1207210086197, 44.5848722561968,
    44.1841282045988, 44.5362420905779, 45.0361888705809, 44.2319254809118,
    44.5027840688528, 44.7154832125319, 43.6450594794842, 43.6096997706505,
    43.7282335656954, 43.2919875395293, 42.7419622107769, 41.6854036117357,
    41.8827495298054
  )
)
library(INLA)
m0 <- inla(y ~ x, family = "gamma", data = ds)
m1 <- inla(y ~ f(x, model = "iid"), family = "gamma", data = ds)
m2 <- inla(y ~ f(x, model = "rw1"), family = "gamma", data = ds)
m3 <- inla(y ~ f(x, model = "rw2"), family = "gamma", data = ds)
m2b <- inla(y ~ f(x, model = "rw1", hyper = list(theta = list(prior = "pc.prec", param = c(0.001, 0.01)))), family = "gamma", data = ds)
m3b <- inla(y ~ f(x, model = "rw2", hyper = list(theta = list(prior = "pc.prec", param = c(0.001, 0.01)))), family = "gamma", data = ds)
